title: When does ML-NMR beat MAIC on error before fitting says so, and what does fitting it cost?
question: In a star network with individual data in one trial, do quantities an analyst can compute before fitting (the transport gap of the aggregate contrasts, overlap, how much of the target law is known) mark where ML-NMR has lower error than MAIC and STC, does that map survive a violated shared effect-modifier assumption, and what fitting burden does multinma impose on the same datasets?
design: Star network of one individual-data and two aggregate trials, binary outcome, external target; transport gap, overlap, target information and shared modification crossed, plus a null cell; MAIC, STC and ML-NMR by paired squared error, multinma fitted on a subsample for burden. 17 cells, 1000 replicates each, 10 multinma fits per cell.
